registry_gates.evidence: One boot is planted under the body and the opposite boot is visibly lifted and displaced with a flexed knee.
The bulky parka and near-frontal torso keep the pelvis and ribcage depth azimuths insufficiently separable; the waist does not expose two unambiguous opposing planes.
The free arm extends toward viewer-right while the head and nose turn toward viewer-left in a coherent counterturn.
At thumbnail scale the figure reads mainly as a planar side lean; limb overlap and foreshortening are not strong enough to establish one unmistakable depth spiral.
